source_evidence: If you do not maintain sufficient cash value to pay your policy’s fees and expenses, your policy may lapse. That means it will terminate without value and your beneficiary will not receive any death benefit. A no-lapse benefit keeps your policy in effect even if you do not have sufficient account value to pay your policy’s fees and expenses.
question: How does a no-lapse benefit differ from a policy lapse?
answer: If cash value is insufficient to cover fees and expenses, a policy may lapse, terminate without value, and provide no death benefit. A no-lapse benefit can keep the policy in effect despite insufficient account value for those charges. Its availability may have conditions, and it may significantly reduce the death benefit.
